_comment: EXAMPLE ONLY. Replace with your real Eduqas DTA criteria and rename this file, then delete this one. The app loads every .md/.txt/.json file in the spec/ folder.
_source: Generic UK A-level Design & Technology NEA expectations. NOT the official Eduqas mark scheme.

criteria.name: Client and problem definition
criteria.description: Identifies a real client or user group and a clearly justified design problem worth solving.
criteria.evidence: A brief naming the client, their needs, and why the problem matters.

criteria.name: Research and analysis
criteria.description: Focused research into existing products, materials, processes and users, analysed rather than merely described, and explicitly linked to the design decisions that follow.
criteria.evidence: Research pages that end in conclusions, not just information.

criteria.name: Design specification
criteria.description: A justified, testable specification derived from the research, with measurable points.
criteria.evidence: Points that can be tested against later, with dimensions or values.

criteria.name: Design ideas and development
criteria.description: A range of initial ideas, then iterative development showing modelling, testing, client feedback and reasoned change.
criteria.evidence: Visible evidence of iteration: what changed, why, and what it fixed.

criteria.name: Manufacturing plan and making
criteria.description: A detailed, sequenced plan with tools, processes, quality checks and safety, followed by clear evidence of manufacture.
criteria.evidence: Stage-by-stage plan and photographs of the making process.

criteria.name: Testing and evaluation
criteria.description: Testing against the specification, honest evaluation of strengths and weaknesses, and specific, justified improvements.
criteria.evidence: Test results, client feedback, and reasoning about what to change.

criteria.name: Communication and presentation
criteria.description: Clear, consistent, well-organised presentation that a moderator can navigate and read easily.
criteria.evidence: Titled pages, readable text, annotated images, consistent typography.
